resolved_findings.evidence: Pilot metadata now requires finite non-boolean [0,1] threshold/NMS values, strict integer class count, lowercase 64-hex checkpoint hash and canonical COCO/generic-vehicle class-ID mapping before base model work. Adversarial subcases include NaN, infinity, boolean threshold, float class count, bad hash, and pedestrian mapping.

Worker reads a bounded alias and selects the pilot adapter from reserved pilot directory name, canonical marker, native pilot schema or pilot min-size field. Missing marker in a custom-named pilot fixture stays Batam adapter and fails unavailable instead of generic fallback.

Bridge validates and allowlists may_be_truncated/max_detections=100; existing response note now warns that reaching the 100-box limit may leave an incomplete count, even when post-cap size filtering leaves fewer boxes. Covered by count=1/truncated=true regression test.

positive_checks: Reviewed bridge/worker/adapter perform no image persistence or traffic-provider requests.
Model and runtime paths originate in trusted server-local configuration; request bytes cannot choose executable/model path.
Bounded subprocess still has no shell; image/response/pixel bounds and sanitized responses remain.
Count policy remains original-image visible-box min-long12/min-short4 after generic NMS; supports no speed, queues or unique flow.
Human certification, production eligibility and Batam validation remain false.
No default promotion receipt was written by reviewer; default-old-model behavior is covered by release tests.

validation.runtime: Repository Python3.12 venv; mocked model work, no detector checkpoint deserialization.

limitations: This is a code/contract review under trusted local server configuration; it does not establish model accuracy, source label correctness or operational production readiness.
Checkpoint/hash verification remains lazy at count time in inherited base service; status metadata availability is not a full inference health check.
